status: Closed — stale baseline no longer reproduces after the subsequent pre-commit extraction; verified green on 2026-09-05
area: A line-budget guard test asserts a threshold its own subject already exceeds at HEAD, so it is red on the mainline
finding: A regression test pins a named module at or below the 600-line budget, and that module is already over the threshold in committed history. The assertion therefore fails on a clean checkout, independently of any working change. A guard that is red before anyone touches the repository carries no signal: it cannot distinguish a regression from the baseline it inherited, every contributor who runs it must first establish that the failure is not theirs, and the natural response after doing that twice is to stop running it. The budget rule itself is sound and was observed doing real work in the same session; the defect is that its enforcement was allowed to enter a permanently failing state rather than failing at the moment the subject crossed the line. This is distinct from the already-recorded claim-admission circularity: there the gate blocks the repair, here the gate has silently stopped guarding.
expectedBehavior: A budget assertion and its subject must not be able to diverge in committed history. Whichever check runs on the mainline should refuse the commit that first pushes a pinned module past its threshold, so the guard can never inherit a failing baseline. Where a baseline genuinely cannot be repaired immediately, the exemption must be explicit, recorded with its own owner and expiry, and visible in the test's own output — an acknowledged and bounded exception, not a red assertion that everyone learns to ignore. State it as the general rule: a guard is only evidence while it is green on an untouched checkout.
evidenceOrRepro: Original 2026-08-16 reproduction was a clean-HEAD failure at 606 lines. Current verification on 2026-09-05: `node --strip-types tests/cli/pre-commit-hook-extraction.test.ts` exited 0 with `hook parity assertions passed`; the previously oversized subject is no longer a failing baseline. No source edit was manufactured for this card.
followUp: Continue enforcing the existing line-budget gate and keep future extraction regressions green. Related to [ATM-BUG-2026-07-29-248] and [ATM-BUG-2026-08-15-003], which cover other budget boundaries.
